Title: Responsible AI and career sustainability: the intersectional role of knowledge, emotion, and capability in Vietnam
Abstract: This study investigates how responsible AI signals (RAS) such as autonomy, justice, beneficence, explainability, and nonmaleficence enhance employees’ career sustainability, with particular focus on dynamic capability, AI emotional response, and AI knowledge management (knowledge sharing, acquisition, and application). Grounded in the Cognition–Affect–Conation (CAC) framework, the study extends its scope from psychology to human resource management by explaining how cognitive, emotional, and behavioral mechanisms jointly shape employees’ responses to responsible AI practices. A quantitative research design was employed using an online questionnaire, gathering responses from a sample of 717 employees in Vietnam and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings reveal that RAS strongly promotes AI emotional response, dynamic capability, and knowledge management processes, including knowledge sharing, acquisition, and application. In turn, AI emotional response, dynamic capability, and the application and sharing of knowledge exert significant positive effects on employee well-being and innovation performance, whereas knowledge acquisition shows no meaningful impact. The study advances theory by integrating the CAC framework with Responsible AI principles to explain how employees adapt and collaborate with AI in organizations. Practically, the findings indicate that adopting responsible AI principles can enhance employee creativity, emotional engagement, and adaptability by promoting knowledge sharing, supportive policies, and transparent AI practices. Managers are encouraged to design learning-oriented environments, continuous AI ethics training, and participatory mechanisms that allow employees to engage with AI fairly and autonomously, thereby fostering well-being, innovation, and long-term career sustainability. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag London Ltd., part of Springer Nature 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于企业环境中员工职业可持续性与负责任AI实践的关系，场景属于人力资源管理与组织行为学，未涉及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范等学术出版领域。
Justification_EN: The study examines responsible AI in the context of employee career sustainability and organizational HRM in Vietnam, with no engagement with academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly publishing norms.

Title: Beyond Engagement: A Multidimensional Framework to Evaluate the Safe Development of Agentic AI in Mental Health
Abstract: The rapid rise of agentic AI in mental health exposes a misalignment between conversational fluency and user safety. We present a multidimensional framework spanning nine evaluation domains—from clinical validity to relational risk and regulatory compliance—designed to assess agentic systems beyond surface metrics. Applying it to eight real-world tools reveals that the most popular agents often lack basic safeguards, while clinically validated solutions remain underutilized. These findings highlight the need for structured oversight and public awareness. Our framework offers a foundation for safer deployment, informed regulation, and design practices grounded in mental health ethics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于心理健康领域中具身AI（agentic AI）的临床安全性与监管，属于医疗伦理场景，不符合纳入标准中‘场景明确限定在学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版领域’的要求，且未涉及AI在学术出版中的伦理或披露问题。

Title: Fair Machine Learning Principles for Ethical and Effective AI-Based Recruitment
Abstract: A growing body of research addressed fundamental ethical concerns for AI-driven recruitment. They Highlight specifically transparency, and accountability concerns. These issues impact highly the fairness and performance of recruitment and consequently the acceptability of AI among end-users particularly candidates as a pivotal stakeholder in the recruitment process. In the absence of appropriate ethical oversight, AI-driven recruitment tools risk delivering discriminatory results, leading to reduce trust and inhibit consequently adoption. The aim of this review is to analyze the impact of bias on the performance and acceptance of the technology to provide a structured approach based on Fair Machine Learning (FairML) principles, which enable a control over ethical challenges. It further explores how FairML principles theoretically frame the key components of responsible AI-based recruitment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦AI在招聘场景中的公平性与伦理问题，属于人力资源/工业应用领域，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’这一严格限定场景。
Justification_EN: The study addresses ethical challenges of AI in recruitment—a human resources and industrial application context—not academic writing, research conduct, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication.

Title: Influence of Artificial Intelligence on Decision-Making in Nursing: An Integrative Review
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming multiple aspects of healthcare, aiming to improve clinical decision-making. However, nursing is no exception, as the adoption of these technologies can present significant challenges in staff training, algorithm reliability, and associated ethical issues. The objective of the research was to analyze the available scientific evidence on the influence of artificial intelligence on decision-making in nursing. The methodology allowed for an integrative review of the scientific literature published in the last 5 years, conducted between January and April 2025, in Scopus, Web Science (WoS), Medline, and Lilacs databases. The health science descriptors (DeCS) “nursing decision making,” “artificial intelligence,” “AI in clinical practice,” “nursing care technology,” “AI ethics,” “AI training for nurses,” and their English equivalents (MeCH) were used, in addition to the Boolean operators AND OR to combine the search, where 14 articles were identified through the rigorous selection criteria established. The results showed a significant influence on the employability of AI in nursing decision-making. The conclusion is that artificial intelligence has transformative potential for the profession, but its acceptance requires an important balance between technological advancement and humanized care. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦AI在护理临床决策中的应用及医疗伦理问题，场景属于医疗实践而非学术写作、期刊发表或学术出版领域，违反纳入标准第3条且符合排除标准第2条（医疗伦理场景）。

Title: Ethical Implications of Black Box AI Models in High-Stakes Applications
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has increasingly been integrated into high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. While these integrations promise significant advancements, they also present substantial ethical challenges, particularly with black box AI models whose decision-making processes are opaque. This paper explores the ethical implications of black box AI in high-stakes applications, focusing on issues such as bias, fairness, accountability, and transparency. Through an in-depth analysis of several case studies—including IBM Watson for Oncology, algorithmic bias in financial lending, and incidents involving autonomous vehicles—we highlight the consequences of opaque AI systems and review current regulatory frameworks. Additionally, we propose comprehensive strategies for addressing ethical concerns, emphasizing the need for enhanced transparency, fairness, and accountability. Our findings suggest that while regulatory and technical advancements are underway, there is a critical need for continued efforts to ensure ethical deployment of AI in high-stakes settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于医疗、金融和自动驾驶等高风险应用中的黑箱AI伦理问题，场景完全不属于学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表或学术出版领域，违反排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: The paper addresses ethical implications of black-box AI in healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems—non-academic-publishing contexts—thus violating Exclusion Criterion 2.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education: Applications, Ethical Challenges, and Strategic Pathways for Institutional Transformation
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, reshaping pedagogical practices, administrative operations, and institutional strategies. This literature review synthesizes recent scholarship (2023–2025) to examine how AI, particularly generative tools such as ChatGPT, is being integrated across global higher education contexts. Findings highlight dual pathways of adoption: pedagogically, AI supports personalized and adaptive learning, intelligent tutoring, content creation, and collaborative learning environments; administratively, it enables data-driven decision-making, resource optimization, and student lifecycle management. While offering significant opportunities, AI adoption raises critical ethical concerns, including academic integrity, data privacy, algorithmic bias, and risks to human development and social interaction. Institutional strategies for effective AI integration emphasize the importance of responsible leadership, robust governance frameworks, faculty development, and infrastructure investment. Student perspectives reveal widespread adoption of AI tools, driven by efficiency and work load pressures, but tempered by concerns about reliability, autonomy, and social consequences. Global analyses underscore disparities in adoption across regions, with most research originating from high-income countries, leaving gaps in understanding cross-cultural and equity-focused implications. The review concludes that AI in higher education is not merely a technological shift but a systemic transformation requiring balanced approaches that align innovation with ethics, efficiency with equity, and automation with human values. Recommendations are offered for institutional leaders, faculty, students, and researchers to guide responsible and sustainable AI implementation in higher education. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽提及‘学术诚信’（academic integrity）这一伦理议题，但其整体场景聚焦于高等教育全系统（含教学、行政、机构治理），未将AI使用披露（AI Disclosure）或出版规范限定在学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版等具体出版环节，不符合纳入标准第3条（场景明确限定在学术出版领域）。

Title: An absurdist ethics of AI: applying Camus’ concepts of rebellion and dignity to the challenges posed by disruptive technoscience
Abstract: This article proposes a new, Camusian approach to analyzing and navigating ethical dilemmas in relation to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and, by extension, to other disruptive technoscience. The article takes as its point of departure the Unified Framework of Five Principles for AI in Society, as advanced by Floridi and Cowls (2021), which offers a comprehensive and cohesive framework of the many abstract values and principles brought up in AI ethics discourse. Using a case-study approach, which focuses on the principle of accountability in AI, we demonstrate that, even following an exhaustive systematization of abstract principles, ethical dilemmas still arise whenever we consider applications of the technology in concrete situations. Furthermore, because of the way technology mediates our ethical judgement, a deeper ethical dilemma arises; we can either judge technologies like AI prematurely, without knowing their impact, or after they have been able to bias our norms and intuitions for ethical deliberation. This article then argues that the vulnerability of our ethical judgement to continuous doubt, which is exposed by AI as a landmark case of disruptive technology, can be addressed by integrating Albert Camus’ philosophy of absurdity, rebellion and dignity. Through Camus, we can contextualize our experience of ethical doubt in relation to AI as existentially absurd, while also navigating normative change more confidently with meta-level principles for ethical deliberation itself. The article concludes that, while ethical dilemmas and doubts will persist, this Camusian approach will make us more responsible in undertaking the continuous adaptation and concretizing of our ethical frameworks. © The Author(s) 2025.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽讨论AI伦理，但聚焦于一般性技术哲学与存在主义伦理框架（卡缪式荒诞理论），未限定于学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范等具体学术出版场景，且未涉及AI使用披露（AI Disclosure）这一核心议题。
Justification_EN: Although the article addresses AI ethics, it develops a general Camusian philosophy of absurdity applied to disruptive technoscience broadly, with no focus on academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, scholarly integrity policies, or AI disclosure requirements in scholarly communication.

Title: Ethical Issues in the Use of Generative AI Chatbots for Therapeutic Purposes
Abstract: This paper discusses the pros and cons related to the digital transformation of mental health, particularly highlighting the therapeutic domain; against this setting, the technical underpinnings of generative AI chatbots are outlined alongside a discussion of the broader ethical and epistemic challenges related to the integration of LLMs in the medical domain —a domain that is more advanced in experimenting with and deploying LLMs than the field of mental health. While focused on mental health, the paper draws on these broader discussions to highlight shared concerns, complemented by insights specific to mental health. Against this backdrop, the paper analyzes AI-based therapy and generative AI companion chatbots, assessing their potential benefits and associated risks, including considerations of relevant European legal frameworks. Following up, the paper argues that even if we succeed in escaping the challenges at the intersection of ethics, episteme, and technology, generative AI chatbots are ill-suited for therapeutic purposes. Playing with the idea of replacing human relationships with “stochastic parrots” risks reducing therapy to algorithmic risk stratification. Such a shift threatens to diminish the potential for cultivating authentic, trust-based therapeutic relationships. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Rethinking Hoffmann’s The Sandman through the lens of AI: human being and robot
Abstract: E.T.A. Hoffmann’s The Sandman (1816) mixed themes such as fear, eeriness and the darkening of the relationship between humans and automatons. The Sandman shows the possible emergence of human machines or so-called artificial intelligence (AI), which is indistinguishable from humans. The paper also looks at emerging and growing technologies, the ethics of artificial life and the nature of consciousness. The technical ability to create automata, developed at the end of the eighteenth century, fascinated nineteenth century authors such as Hoffmann. In The Sandman, Olimpia embodies the nineteenth century fascination with machines and mechanical beings that can imitate and interact with humans. Olimpia is the epitome of the modern concept of AI, in which machines simulate and control human behavior in various capacities. This paper is about how The Sandman anticipates the human ability to understand the nature of reality and technology. With the advent of mass media and the development of AI, I show how the protagonist Nathaniel complicates the conceptualization of the human subject. By relying on and compromising with technology, Nathaniel loses his humanity and turns himself into a madman. The paper also highlights the text and compares it to contemporary AI narratives. Fear and anxiety, reflections on the loss of humanity in the face of technological advancement and the potential of AI to surpass human intelligence are also discussed. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag London Ltd., part of Springer Nature 2025.
Justification_ZH: 该文献将AI作为文学隐喻分析霍夫曼小说中的人机关系与人性异化，未涉及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版政策等学术/出版场景，也未讨论AI在科研中的伦理使用或披露要求。
Justification_EN: The paper uses AI as a literary metaphor to analyze human-robot relations and dehumanization in Hoffmann's fiction, with no engagement whatsoever with academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, scholarly integrity practices, or AI disclosure requirements in research or publication contexts.

Title: Artificial Intelligence toward Sustainable Impact Accelerator through Education, Research, and Advocacy: Critical Assessments
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a defining force of the 21st century, influencing almost every dimension of human life. Its rapid evolution not only reshapes industries but also redefines how societies think about education, research, and advocacy. This chapter explores the role of AI as a sustainable impact accelerator, with a focus on its integration into teaching and learning (T&L), research advancement, and policy advocacy. Unlike earlier technological shifts, AI—particularly generative AI—does not merely act as a tool but increasingly functions as a partner that augments human creativity, decision-making, and problem-solving capacity. In the context of education, AI tools such as adaptive learning platforms, automated assessment systems, and generative AI models (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) provide students and educators with new ways of engaging with knowledge, tailoring learning experiences, and promoting inclusivity across diverse backgrounds. Within research, AI accelerates discovery by streamlining data analysis, modeling complex systems, and enabling interdisciplinary collaborations, thereby shortening the time from hypothesis to application. In advocacy, AI enhances outreach and evidence-based policy design by analyzing large volumes of social, economic, and environmental data, which can inform sustainable strategies and inclusive decision-making. At the same time, the integration of AI raises concerns regarding ethics, equity, transparency, and long-term societal implications. Addressing these challenges requires a balanced approach that emphasizes human oversight, digital literacy, and responsible-use policies. The chapter argues that AI can serve as a transformative accelerator for sustainable impact only when deployed thoughtfully and guided by principles of inclusivity, accountability, and shared benefit. By examining concrete applications, potential impacts, and future pathways, this work provides a roadmap for leveraging AI across education, research, and advocacy, with the goal of fostering a more sustainable, equitable, and human-centered future. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, Samsul Ariffin Abdul Karim, Chockalingam Aravind Vaithilingam and Ari Happonen; individual chapters, the contributors.
Justification_ZH: 虽提及AI在研究中的应用及伦理关切，但未聚焦学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范中的AI披露（AI Disclosure）问题，而是泛化讨论教育、研究和倡导三大领域中的可持续影响与原则性伦理，不符合‘场景明确限定在学术出版领域’的纳入标准。
Justification_EN: Although it mentions ethical concerns and AI use in research, it does not focus on AI disclosure, academic integrity, or publishing norms within scholarly writing, journal submission, peer review, or academic publishing—instead treating 'research' as a broad societal domain rather than the scholarly communication process, thus failing the required contextual specificity for inclusion.

Title: CL-GIE v4.0: Blockchain-Anchored Cross-Layer Genomic Integrity With Hierarchical Bloom–Merkle Trees for Ethics-Aware, Explainable Personalized Gene Editing
Abstract: Personalized gene editing demands verifiable integrity, governance-aware decisioning, and forensics-grade auditability across heterogeneous evidence sources (CRISPR logs, phenotype outcomes, and ledger records). We present CL-GIE v4.0, a cross-layer genomic integrity evaluator that fuses: 1) a Hierarchical Bloom–Merkle Tree (HBMT) for O(log N) membership proofs and vertical consistency; 2) an entropy–KL drift channel that detects distributional shifts across temporal, phenotypic, and edit-type features; 3) lightweight structural checks (timestamp monotonicity, hash replay); and 4) an interpretable ethics policy engine. HBMT yields succinct proofs (depth ≈ 14 on our test set) with verified roots, enabling forensics-ready attestations and chain anchoring. CL-GIE operates under tight latency budgets: per-record HBMT verification is ~0.02  ms, while meta-model scoring remains sub-millisecond, sustaining real-time pipelines. Empirically, CL-GIE surpasses one-class, reconstruction, clustering, and rules baselines. A stacked variant attains state-of-the-art ROC (AUC = 0.991), while isotonic meta-calibration maximizes area under the precision–recall curve (AP = 0.852), reflecting robustness at low prevalence. Confusion matrices corroborate high recall and specificity (e.g., stacked: TP = 480, FN = 23, TN = 9398, FP = 99), aligning with clinical detection priorities and low false-positive exposure. An ablation-driven weight sweep shows that ethics signals and cross-layer drift are pivotal at the optimal operating point, with validation F1  ≈  0.81–0.88 across calibrated and stacked settings. Radar and correlation analyses further indicate balanced gains across AUROC, AUPR, F1, specificity, and calibration metrics. Overall, CL-GIE delivers a principled, explainable, and audit-capable integrity layer for ethically governed gene-editing workflows, unifying cryptographic proofs, drift-aware detection, and policy transparency under a single evaluative framework. © 2013 IEEE.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于基因编辑中的区块链与密码学完整性验证，其‘ethics-aware’指临床/生物医学研究伦理（如基因编辑治理），场景属于医疗健康领域，不符合‘学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’的限定场景。
Justification_EN: The paper addresses genomic integrity and ethics-aware governance in personalized gene editing—a biomedical/clinical application domain—not academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication, thus violating the scenario-specific inclusion criterion.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chain Optimization for Efficiency, Resilience, and Sustainability
Abstract: The rise in globalizing the market, the grow in customers expectations and esca lating uncertain events, including pandemic, have driven the companies towards becoming more efficient and resilient in their supply chains. AI: An algorithm to transform supply chain optimization Artificial Intelligence (AI) remarkable becomes a disrupter of supply chain optimization that is reality- tested to assist predictive analytics, demand forecast, inventory management, transportation planning and real- time decision making. Supply chains are about to change to be agile, trans parent and sustainable in the wake of integration of AI and other technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, IoT(Internet of thing) and blockchain. The chapter lays the principles of AI into the supply chain and implication to real istic optimisation strategies, industry enablers and industry case studies to show practical applications. It explores the adoption barriers - data privacy, ethics and workforce - and presents future trends and directions, e.g. autonomic supply chains and generative AI- inspired design. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽提及‘ethics’作为AI在供应链中应用的采纳障碍之一，但其核心议题是供应链优化的技术应用，场景完全属于工业/商业运营领域，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’的限定场景。
Justification_EN: Although ethics is briefly mentioned as an adoption barrier, the study's core focus is on AI-driven supply chain optimization in industrial and commercial operations, not in academic writing, research, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication.

Title: A Strategic Roadmap for the Adoption and Operational Integration of Robot-Assisted Surgery in Modern Healthcare Systems
Abstract: Robot-assisted surgery (RAS) has witnessed a rapid expansion in recent years, further accelerated by the emergence of Healthcare 5.0 and its enabling technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. These advancements have significantly improved critical areas such as surgical training, image segmentation, and classification. Despite this growing adoption, healthcare institutions still lack a structured and comprehensive roadmap (RM) to guide the implementation and operational management of RAS (OM-RAS). This study aims to develop a robust RM to support healthcare facilities in effectively integrating RAS into clinical practice. Two main research questions are addressed: (1) What are the essential requirements for successful RAS implementation? and (2) What defines a practical and reliable framework for managing RAS operations? The contributions of this study are twofold: first, it offers a structured seven-theme roadmap for OM-RAS that centers technology and infrastructure (segmentation, kinematic modeling, AI tools, advanced control), links these with implementation, ethics–legal, and training/HR, and specifies initial integration steps aligned with Healthcare 4.0/5.0 (telesurgery, 6G, integrated AI, cybersecurity). Second, it sets an analytics-driven agenda that quantifies inter-theme dependencies to forecast workflow variability and optimize scheduling, resource allocation, and team assignment under real-world constraints. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽提及AI工具和‘伦理–法律’（ethics–legal）作为RAS实施框架的一个主题，但其核心议题是机器人辅助手术在医疗系统中的临床整合与运营管理，场景明确属于医疗临床实践而非学术写作、期刊发表或学术出版领域，违反纳入标准第3条且符合排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: Although the paper mentions 'ethics–legal' as one component of a robot-assisted surgery (RAS) implementation framework, its core focus is on clinical integration and operational management of RAS in healthcare delivery—not academic writing, research conduct, journal publishing, or peer review—thus failing the domain-specific inclusion criterion (3) and satisfying exclusion criterion (2).

Title: Redefining Academic Integrity in the Age of AI: Ethics and Security in Academic Content Creation
Abstract: Redefining academic integrity in an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven world is now a pressing issue for higher education. This paper examines the implications of AI on academic integrity in higher education, focusing on how AI tools challenge traditional notions of originality, authorship, and ethical accountability in academic content creation. The shift in focus is from detection and punishment to ethics and pedagogy, guided by the notion of enabling students to use AI ethically. Case studies from Southeast Asia reveal how institutions are responding to AI concerns with inclusive pedagogies, disclosure-based policies, and frameworks for transparency and accountability. This paper argues that academic integrity accounts for the needs of diverse learners to support equitable access to institutional learning opportunities and resources. Institutions need to make the necessary changes to continuously adapt to the rapid development of AI technologies. By reimagining academic integrity, higher education can uphold its responsibilities in an AI-driven future. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.
Justification_ZH: 该文献明确以AI在学术内容创作中的伦理、学术诚信和披露型政策（disclosure-based policies）为核心议题，场景严格限定在高等教育中的学术写作与出版相关实践，完全满足全部三项纳入标准。
Justification_EN: The paper explicitly centers on ethics, academic integrity, and disclosure-based policies for AI use in academic content creation within higher education, squarely addressing the scholarly writing and publishing context while meeting all three inclusion criteria.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Law Enforcement Training in Mongolia’s Higher Education: Current State and Challenges
Abstract: The use of artificial intelligence is rapidly being integrated into higher education operations, and by applying AI to the teaching and research processes, quality, while having a positive impact on enhancing quality and productivity in the teaching and research processes, it continues to pose significant challenges to ethics, integrity, and information security. The research investigates how law enforcement university cadets and faculty members use artificial intelligence systems and examines their related opinions. The scope of this study is limited to the faculty members and cadets, and the data were collected by using a questionnaire. The questions were divided into five key sections: the use of artificial intelligence, academic ethics, integrity, the impact on instructional quality, safety of the data information, and future trends. While there was no significant difference in the use of AI by faculty members and cadets based on the specifics of the law enforcement sector, the potential for data privacy and risks related to false information is much greater due to the specifics of the sector. Furthermore, a mutual or united understanding of academic dishonesty, which could serve as the researcher’s ethical principle guideline, has not yet been formed. And this is directly related to the state in which the university has no rules or regulations governing the use of AI. Therefore, the university must generate and implement governing rules and regulations related to the use of AI that are based on the core principles of the law enforcement sector: information truth and correctness, confidentiality, ethics, and integrity. © 2026 Amartogtokh Battulga, et al.
Justification_ZH: 该研究场景聚焦于蒙古国高等教育中执法培训领域的人工智能应用，核心关切是执法教育中的数据隐私、虚假信息风险及部门特定伦理（如信息真实性、保密性），而非学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范等学术出版场景。
Justification_EN: The study focuses on AI use in law enforcement training within higher education—not academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication—and centers on sector-specific concerns (e.g., information truth, confidentiality in policing), not AI disclosure, research integrity, or publishing ethics in scholarly contexts.

Title: The Next Frontier in AI: Speech as a Digital Biomarker
Abstract: Dr. Fasih Haider FBCS, Research Fellow at the Usher Institute, University of Edinburgh and Entrepreneurial Lead at Innovate UK ICURe Program, explains how AI can analyse how we speak to detect early signs of neurological and mental health conditions, and also highlights important considerations around bias, regulation and ethics.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦AI在神经与精神健康领域作为数字生物标志物的临床应用，涉及的伦理议题属于医疗伦理范畴，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’这一严格限定场景。
Justification_EN: The study addresses AI's use in clinical neurological/mental health diagnostics and associated ethics, falling under medical ethics—not academic writing, research conduct, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication as required.

Title: AI and Digital Innovation in Healthcare Reform: From Policy to Practice
Abstract: AI and digital innovation bridge the gap between healthcare policy design and real-world practice. From predictive analytics and telemedicine to automated diagnostics and data-driven decision-making, these technologies reshape how care is delivered, managed, and evaluated. As governments and institutions implement policies to modernize healthcare systems, the integration of AI introduces opportunities for improved efficiency and outcomes, and challenges related to ethics, equity, and data privacy. Understanding how these innovations impact everyday use may build more responsive, accessible, and sustainable healthcare systems. AI and Digital Innovation in Healthcare Reform: From Policy to Practice explores how AI and digital technologies shape healthcare reform from policy development to practical implementation. It examines the benefits and challenges of integrating these innovations into healthcare systems, including their impact on efficiency, accessibility, ethics, and patient outcomes. This book covers topics such as social media, women’s health, and medical technologies, and is a useful resource for medical and healthcare professionals, engineers, academicians, researchers, and scientists. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.
Justification_ZH: 该文献场景明确属于医疗健康改革与临床实践，聚焦AI在预测分析、远程医疗和自动诊断中的应用，虽提及伦理与数据隐私，但完全脱离学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范等限定场景，违反排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: The study is explicitly situated in healthcare reform and clinical practice—addressing predictive analytics, telemedicine, and automated diagnostics—without any focus on academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication norms, thus violating Exclusion Criterion 2.

Title: The Reskilling Imperative: Redefining Software Engineering Skills in the Age of AI-Generated Code
Abstract: The fact of artificial intelligence gaining ground along with its instant progress with artificial intelligence as a particular example of the given phenomenon fundamentally changes the situation in software engineering. This chapter discusses the rising reskilling demand with developers leaving behind conventional coding jobs and moving into more agile, artificially intelligent jobs. It discusses the influence that tools that are run on large language models have had on the development processes, particularly how they are now prioritizing problem-solving, system design, and code validation rather than manual code writing. The discussion indicates the changes in the skills requirements such as instant engineering, critical thinking and the sense of ethics, as well as the essential value of the basic knowledge of programming. Besides, the chapter examines the implication in education, workforce development as well as organizational training where the continuity of learning and curriculum modification are paramount. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦软件工程从业者技能重塑与教育转型，虽提及‘伦理感’（sense of ethics），但未将伦理议题锚定在学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范等限定场景中，且核心讨论对象是AI生成代码对开发流程和职业能力的影响，不符合纳入标准第3条（场景限定）。
Justification_EN: The study addresses AI-generated code's impact on software engineering practice and workforce reskilling, mentioning 'sense of ethics' only generically without linking ethics or AI disclosure to academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly publishing norms—thus failing inclusion criterion #3 (scene restriction).

Title: Ethical, Legal and Societal Implications of AI in Neurology and Medicine
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has established an influential force in neurology and medicine. It has spurred the progress of diagnosis, treatment planning and management of patients. Predictive analytics, machine-learning algorithms and natural language processing have become a part of clinical practice. These technologies provide superior medical results, increase operational efficiency, as well as personal care. This chapter provides a complete overview of the ethical, legal and social concerns regarding AI in neurology and medicine. It focuses on the potential and the threats. The chapter compiles relevant literature, providing an overall picture of the AI changes in healthcare. It also emphasizes the importance of powerful systems, which should balance responsibility and innovativeness. These issues need to be discussed so that AI can positively affect the care conditions of patients, promote medical ethics and contribute to the society. © ISTE Ltd 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于神经病学与医学临床场景中的AI伦理、法律及社会影响，属于医疗伦理范畴，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’这一严格限定场景。
Justification_EN: The study addresses ethical, legal, and societal implications of AI specifically in clinical neurology and medicine — a healthcare delivery context — and thus fails the exclusion criterion prohibiting non-academic-publishing scenarios.

Title: Compensation for Damage Caused by the Use of Artificial Intelligence Application
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly embedded in critical sectors such as healthcare and finance, raising new challenges for legal accountability. This paper investigates whether current legal frameworks adequately protect users from economic and non-economic harm caused by AI systems. Using doctrinal legal analysis and comparative insights from EU and common law jurisdictions, the study examines tort law, data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR), consumer protection rules, and soft law instruments like ethics charters. Through a critical review of legislation, case law, and regulatory proposals, particularly the EU AI Act—the research reveals significant gaps in assigning liability for AI-related harm. Opaque and autonomous AI decision-making often impedes causation analysis, leaving victims undressed. Existing tort and product liability doctrines fall short of ensuring consumer protection. The paper proposes reforms, including strict liability for high-risk AI, insurance-based compensation schemes, and legal personhood for AI to address these issues. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于AI在医疗、金融等领域的法律归责与损害赔偿问题，属于法律AI与产品责任范畴，未涉及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范中的AI伦理与披露议题，违反排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: The paper addresses legal liability and compensation for AI-induced harm in healthcare and finance—falling under legal AI and product liability—not academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or publishing ethics/disclosure, thus violating Exclusion Criterion 2.

Title: Moral Suspension in Human-GenAI Interaction: Scale Development and Validation for Chinese Emerging Adults
Abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has introduced unprecedented ethical complexity into contemporary human-GenAI collaboration, especially among emerging adults (individuals aged 18–29). Traditional moral theories emphasize users’ active rationalization processes but do not fully capture the passive ethical ambiguity that arises in interactions with opaque and autonomous GenAI systems. To address this gap, this study introduces and operationalizes the construct of Moral Suspension, defined as a psychological state characterized by interactive environmental complexity, ambiguity in responsibility attribution, and passive responsibility exemption during GenAI-assisted tasks. Guided by social cognitive theory, we developed the Moral Suspension Scale (MSS) and employed a rigorous multi-phase validation process, including expert review, pilot testing, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and measurement invariance assessment. Data were collected from Chinese emerging adults (n = 785) with practical experience in AI-assisted academic or creative activities. The finalized MSS consists of 38 items and demonstrates strong reliability, model fit, and invariance across gender. The MSS provides a robust instrument for assessing moral psychological ambiguity in GenAI contexts, advancing theoretical integration between moral psychology and human-GenAI interaction. This research contributes an empirical foundation for the ethical evaluation of GenAI and offers practical guidance for responsible system design and digital ethics education for younger generations. © 2026 The Author(s). Published with license by Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Justification_ZH: 该文献明确以GenAI在学术或创意活动中的使用为背景，聚焦‘道德悬置’这一新型伦理心理状态，核心议题为AI辅助任务中的责任归属模糊与伦理模糊性，直接关联学术场景下的AI伦理与披露前提（即使用者对AI介入的意识、归责能力及潜在披露动因），符合纳入标准中‘AI技术+学术场景+伦理/披露’三重限定。
Justification_EN: The study explicitly examines moral ambiguity (Moral Suspension) in GenAI-assisted academic or creative activities among emerging adults, centering on responsibility attribution and ethical passivity—core ethical concerns directly relevant to AI disclosure expectations and integrity in academic writing and publishing.

Title: Agentic AI for Therapy
Abstract: Existing Large Language Model (LLM) based systems for mental health support are often unsafe and unreliable, primarily due to the absence of dynamic, user-controlled memory. This limitation leads to inconsistent therapeutic continuity and undermines the user trust necessary for forming meaningful therapeutic alliances. This paper introduces an Agentic Therapeutic Agent designed to address these challenges through a modular architecture that prioritizes safety, transparency, and long-term relationship building. The proposed framework's core feature is a secure Long-Term Memory system with a user-facing control panel and pathways for human therapist oversight. Initial development has produced two foundational, non-integrated modules: a rudimentary conversational AI and an effective crisis detection model intended to function as the first component of the agent's Safety & Guardrail Layer. The central contribution of this project is the design, implementation, and validation of this transparent memory architecture, which will integrate the conversational and safety modules. This approach directly addresses the critical gaps of memory and trust in therapeutic AI, demonstrating a tangible pathway toward a more ethically guided and effective support tool. © 2026 IEEE.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦AI在心理治疗场景中的安全与信任设计，属于医疗健康应用，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’的限定场景，触犯排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: The study addresses ethical design of AI for mental health therapy, which falls under clinical/healthcare application—not academic writing, research, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication—thus violating Exclusion Criterion 2.

Title: Ethical, Pedagogical, and Research Implications of AI Use in Education and Academic Research
Abstract: The evolution of AI has transformed education and academic research. It powers several academic tasks, such as teaching, learning, implementing research, and research writing. For example, generative AI could produce human-like outputs in response to user input, such as providing constructive feedback, outlines key research interests in a particular area, and summarizing an input text. However, researchers and practitioners have raised concerns about possible risks of AI. Central to these concerns are ethics, accountability, and integrity. Acknowledging the current concepts about AI use, this chapter contributes to the still limited literature on ethical use of AI. The chapter first provides an overall landscape of AI use in education and academic research, showing both potentials and achievements of AI before raising ethical concerns about responsible AI use. Subsequently, we outlines issues regarding the AI use in the academic world, arguing for the roles of policy and guidelines. Finally, we outlines issues that the future generations of AI should respond to. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献明确以‘学术研究’为场景，核心议题聚焦于AI使用的伦理、问责与诚信问题，并特别论及AI在研究写作中的应用及政策指南需求，完全满足三项纳入标准。
Justification_EN: The paper explicitly centers on 'academic research' as its context, directly addresses ethics, accountability, and integrity of AI use—including in research writing—and advocates for policies and guidelines, fully satisfying all three inclusion criteria.

Title: Causal, Strategic, and Combined Responsibility Attribution in Situation Calculus Concurrent Game Structures
Abstract: Responsibility is a central concept in accountable decision making for multiagent systems. As modern AI systems grow in complexity and autonomy, there is a growing demand for them to address issues in AI ethics, prompting researchers to formalize responsibility from diverse perspectives, including strategic responsibility. However, causal responsibility, i.e. responsibility due to actual causal contribution, has received much less attention. In this paper, we study variants of responsibility attribution from both strategic and causal perspectives within a synchronous game-theoretic logic framework that allows concurrent moves by multiple agents. Our formalization is based on Situation Calculus Synchronous Game Structures (SCSGS). We show that by combining these perspectives, one can obtain novel forms of responsibility attribution that are grounded on actual causation. While doing this, we propose an account of actual causation in SCSGS. We prove that our formalization handles the issues associated with preemption and over-determination well. We also study some key properties of responsibility and demonstrate that causal, strategic, and combined notions of responsibility are extensionally distinct. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). All rights reserved.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于多智能体系统中责任归属的形式化逻辑建模（因果责任与策略责任），虽提及AI伦理背景，但未涉及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范中的AI使用披露问题，场景完全脱离学术出版领域。
Justification_EN: The paper formalizes responsibility attribution in multiagent systems using game-theoretic logic and Situation Calculus, with only a generic reference to AI ethics; it does not address AI disclosure, academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or any aspect of scholarly publishing practice.

Title: Digital Hospitals: How the Metaverse is Reshaping Healthcare Services
Abstract: The rapid integration of metaverse technology into healthcare is transforming medical services by establishing digital hospitals, enhancing telemedicine, and introducing immersive virtual reality-driven treatments. By incorporating unconventional technologies like VR, AR, AI, and Blockchain, digital hospitals reshape patient care delivery, medical training, and healthcare accessibility. From remote consultations to AI-assisted surgeries and blockchain secured medical records, the metaverse is enabling a paradigm shift in how healthcare professionals interact with patients, manage data, and deliver services in a virtual environment. This paper explores the vast opportunities digital hospitals present, including improved healthcare accessibility, cost-effective solutions, enhanced medical training, and AI-powered precision diagnostics. Furthermore, it critically examines the security and ethical challenges related with metaverse driven healthcare, such as patient data privacy, cybersecurity risks, digital inequality, and the AI ethics implications in medical decision-making. As digital hospitals become an integral part of the healthcare landscape, it has been crucial to evolve regulatory frameworks, ethical guidelines & technological safeguards to ensure their responsible and inclusive deployment. By analyzing real-world case studies and emerging technologies, this re-search provides an extensive summation about how the metaverse can be effectively harnessed to improve healthcare outcomes while addressing ethical dilemmas and security concerns. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽提及AI伦理，但场景明确限定在医疗健康服务（如AI辅助手术、医疗决策），属于排除标准中明确列出的‘医疗伦理’非学术出版场景。
Justification_EN: Although AI ethics is mentioned, the context is strictly healthcare delivery (e.g., AI-assisted surgery, medical decision-making), falling squarely under the exclusion criterion of 'medical ethics' — a non-academic-publishing scenario.

Title: AI Ontological Freedom (as a Limit for Its Regulation)
Abstract: The ethics of Artificial Intelligence can be approached from different levels, from the operational and structural to the ontological. Each of these levels addresses different problems, ranging from simpler and more immediate issues such as operational issues related to the application of AI in industry, to more subtle and complex issues such as biases in Artificial Intelligence models, or the social and environmental repercussions of the development of these technologies. All these aspects require ethical reflection and legal complementarity in the form of rights and regulations that allow for the proper assimilation of the technology. However, none of these perspectives exhausts the reflection on Artificial Intelligence itself as an intelligent entity. The chapter refers to the philosophies of Deleuze and Guattari, Yuk Hui, and Negarestani to understand Artificial Intelligence (and in particular the generative one) as the result of a process of technical development that is coupled with the social and the ontological and that, in order to be completed, must address the radical autonomy of the machine, its ontological freedom, as a requirement for its realization. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于AI本体论自由等哲学层面的抽象思辨，未涉及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范中的伦理与AI披露问题，违反纳入标准第2、3条。
Justification_EN: The paper engages in abstract philosophical inquiry into AI's 'ontological freedom' without addressing ethics, disclosure, academic integrity, or publishing practices in scholarly writing, peer review, or journal publication, thus failing inclusion criteria 2 and 3.

Title: From ethics washing to enforceable accountability: hospitals as hubs of digital constitutionalism
Abstract: The governance of artificial intelligence (AI) in European healthcare reveals a structural paradox. While the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) classifies most medical AI systems as high-risk and imposes extensive obligations on providers and deployers, the institutional mechanisms meant to enforce these obligations often remain merely advisory. This article conceptualizes this disjunction as the enforceability gap: the systemic mismatch between formal legal responsibility and the institutional capacity to exercise coercive authority. This paper, in bridging insights from accountability theory, risk governance, and digital constitutionalism, argues that enforceability constitutes the missing link between algorithmic authority and democratic legitimacy. Authority without enforceability, it contends, results in symbolic governance, where ethics boards simulate oversight without power to constrain decisions. To overcome this deficit, the paper proposes a model of enforceable accountability grounded in four pillars: legally empowered institutional boards with conditional veto powers; corporate and professional liability mechanisms; transparency and restorative-oriented frameworks; and participatory procedures embedding democratic deliberation. The paper’s key innovation is to re-center hospitals as one-stop accountability hubs—integrated institutional loci where ethical review, legal compliance, and technical audit converge within a unified governance structure. By conceptualizing hospitals as active co-regulators rather than passive deployers, the paper demonstrates how enforceable accountability can be operationalized at the point of clinical implementation. In this perspective, addressing the enforceability gap is not solely a matter of regulatory refinement, but a structural condition for aligning high-risk AI governance with the rule-of-law requirements of the European digital order, ensuring that ethical obligations acquire effective legal force rather than remaining aspirational norms. © The Author(s) 2026.

Justification_EN: The article addresses AI governance in European healthcare settings—specifically hospitals as accountability hubs for clinical AI deployment—and falls squarely under medical ethics and regulatory enforcement, not academic writing, research integrity, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication.

Title: Digital human twins for disabled people: technology for enabling or ableism?
Abstract: Amongst disruptive technologies in twenty-first century, digital twinning has been the backbone of the industry 4.0. This technology has also been increasingly applied to medicine and precision public health by creating digital human twins (DHT). However, the transformative nature of this technology also brings social and societal implications. This article addresses the research question of ‘What are the social implications of DHT development and the accompanying discourse in relation to disability?’ by critically reviewing and discussing the implications of the technology for disabled people and for their work and employment. In doing so, we fundamentally take socio-technical view which has dual focus on excellence in technology development as well as the equality that is afforded to people. Two key sociological theories underpin our discussion, namely 1) socio-materiality in the light of agentic capacity of DHT; and 2) technoableism and epistemic injustice rooted in critical disability study. Our aim of the paper is to offer provoking yet helpful points to think in addressing questions around the social implications of the DHT development to the disabled people. We raise novel questions of ethics on AI and DHT based on our arguments regarding agentic capacity of the technology and epistemic injustice faced by disabled people. We conclude our paper by suggesting the potential for DHT to be used to enhance disabled people’s well-being and sense of togetherness in the workplace and the society. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag London Ltd., part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Algorithms for Smart World Technologies: A Comprehensive Guide to Applications in AI, IoT and Automation for Electrical and Computer Engineers
Abstract: Enables readers to learn how to design and implement algorithms for efficient and secure smart technologies Algorithms for Smart World Technologies explains the fundamentals of key algorithms and their application in a variety of use cases, covering the factors, assumptions, and models essential for the design of a real-world algorithm and discussing the importance of advanced algorithms in the use of modern world technologies such as AI, IoT, and Blockchain. Each chapter is written to provide a self-contained treatment of one major topic. Collectively, the chapters have been designed and carefully integrated to be entirely complementary with respect to definitions, terminology, and notation. Chapters are divided into three parts-complexities, paradigms, and recent applications-and at the beginning of each part, a detailed introduction explaining each subject area is provided. The foundational subjects are supported by end-of-chapter exercises and case studies, while the application-focused chapters are supported by projects to give worked experience. Written by two highly qualified authors in academia, sample topics covered in Algorithms for Smart World Technologies include: • Complexities, including complex systems and algorithms, measuring efficiency, types of systems, and types of complexities • Ethics bounds, including algorithms ethics maps, algorithmic traceability, social ethics, environmental ethics, and parameters and thresholds • Algorithmic paradigms, including the design of an algorithm, the divide and conquer algorithm, backtracking, exhaustive search, solvability, and reducibility • Intelligent search algorithms, including solution space, uninformed, and informed search algorithms, evolutionary algorithms, and nature-inspired algorithms • Smart transportation, including scheduling algorithms for vehicular traffic and opportunistic communication for VANET Written for developers and domain experts who want to explore the opportunities and challenges of designing and developing algorithms and protocols for Smart-world problems, Algorithms for Smart World Technologies is an authoritative resource on the topic that provides both foundational knowledge and guidance on practical applications. © 2026 by John Wiley & Sons, Inc. All rights reserved, including rights for text and data mining and training of artificial intelligence technologies or similar technologies.

Title: From Cogwheels to Concepts: A Perspective on the Interplay of Robotics and Ontology
Abstract: The hard problems of robotics occur at the interface of an artificial agent and its surrounding physical world: perception and action. These are often regarded as tasks requiring tacit, unformalized and possibly unformalizable knowledge, making ontology engineering of apparently little value for robotics. We argue instead that an important role has appeared for ontology in current developments in robotics. Recent AI techniques such as foundation models have revealed the potential of explicit knowledge to be useful at all parts of a robotic system, but these techniques will require assistance from formal, verifiable methods to produce trustworthy systems. Further, robotics can contribute to the development of ontology engineering. As robotic agents become more autonomously capable, questions about the meaning of agency and responsibility become increasingly pressing, and will require careful consensus building across a variety of stakeholder groups. Finally, robotics may be a challenging test ground for the philosophical assumptions underlying foundational ontologies, and can thus assist the ontology engineering community in better understanding the consequences of ontological modeling decisions more generally. © The Author(s) 2026
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦机器人学与本体论的哲学和技术交叉，核心议题是 ontology engineering 在物理世界智能体（机器人）中的应用及对哲学假设的检验，未涉及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或AI使用披露等学术出版场景，且未讨论AI在学术诚信、伦理规范或披露要求方面的具体问题。
Justification_EN: The paper addresses the philosophical and technical interplay between robotics and ontology engineering—centering on perception, action, agency, and foundational assumptions—not AI ethics, disclosure requirements, academic integrity, or publishing practices in scholarly contexts.

Title: Engineering Ethics of AI by Design: Principles, Practices, and Frameworks for Responsible Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: This book addresses the growing need for ethical considerations in the development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems. As AI technologies continue to advance at an unprecedented pace, they bring transformative benefits across industries but also raise significant ethical challenges, such as bias, accountability, transparency, and societal impact. This book bridges the gap between theoretical ethical principles and practical engineering practices, offering a comprehensive guide for embedding ethics into the AI development lifecycle. By focusing on actionable frameworks, case studies, and engineering-centric approaches, the book equips readers with the tools to design and implement AI systems that are not only innovative but also responsible and aligned with societal values. © The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

Title: Balancing Technology and Human Expertise: An Industry Perspective on AI Integration in Housekeeping Operations
Abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation has transformed housekeeping operations in hospitality. Technology streamlines routine tasks, enhances efficiency, and promotes sustainability, yet the human element remains vital for service quality and guest personalization. This study, based on a survey of 67 Indian hospitality organizations, explores how AI and human expertise complement each other. Findings show AI improves process optimization, speed, and decision-making, while humans ensure empathy, ethics, and cultural sensitivity. Challenges include data privacy, workforce adaptability, and continuous upskilling. Balancing innovation with human values is essential for sustainable growth and superior guest experiences. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.
Justification_ZH: 该文献场景为酒店业客房服务运营，属于工业/服务业应用，不符合“学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版”这一严格限定场景。
Justification_EN: The study focuses on AI integration in housekeeping operations within the hospitality industry, which falls outside the required academic/research publishing context (e.g., scholarly writing, peer review, journal publication).

Title: Generative AI for Synthetic Data Creation in Privacy-Preserving Data Analytics
Abstract: With increasing reliance on data analytics across industries, the bar of concern for privacy and data security has reached an all-time high. At this point, synthetic data becomes relevant as a developing solution to the anchored problems regulatory and ethical concerns cast upon organizations. Synthetic data can present statistical properties of real-world data generated by generative AI models while keeping sensitive information private. Namely, GANs and VAEs, among other advanced AI models, are potent frameworks for creating synthetic high-quality datasets. These models enable the generation of data that conciliates between privacy and utility to support analytics with privacy preservation without hurting analytical performance. Integrating differential privacy with federated learning for the generated AI further strengthens protection against data breaches and re-identification risks. However, concerns remain regarding biased generative models, ethics, and the trade-off between data fidelity and privacy. This study discusses the capabilities of generative AI in generating synthetic data, the implications for privacy-preserving analytics, ethical dilemmas, and further research. A scheme is developed to effectively utilize generative AI in this area, which again leads to a demand for more innovation and interdisciplinary work. Synthetic data creation through generative AI will revolutionize how data will be shared in the years to come securely, ethically, and efficiently for analytics in modern times. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽提及‘ethics’，但其核心议题是生成式AI在隐私保护数据分析中的技术应用（如GANs、VAEs、差分隐私、联邦学习），场景聚焦于工业/跨行业数据安全与分析，而非学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版中的AI伦理与披露问题。
Justification_EN: Although ethics is mentioned, the study's core focus is on the technical application of generative AI (e.g., GANs, VAEs, differential privacy, federated learning) for privacy-preserving data analytics in industrial and cross-sectoral contexts, not on AI ethics, disclosure requirements, or publishing norms within academic research, scholarly writing, peer review, or journal publication.

Title: AI Governance, Law, Policy and Ethics in Green Finance and ESG
Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into green finance and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) frameworks reshapes how sustainability is measured, managed, and enforced. Governance, law, policy, and ethics are critical in guiding the responsible use of AI for climate risk assessment, sustainable investing, and corporate accountability. Robust regulatory frameworks may ensure transparency, fairness, and data integrity, while addressing ethical concerns like bias, greenwashing, and unequal access to technological resources. By aligning innovation with accountability, this field underscores how AI can support more credible, efficient, and equitable pathways toward sustainable development. AI Governance, Law, Policy and Ethics in Green Finance and ESG explores the integration of AI in green finance and ESG practices, and the evolving governance, legal, and policy frameworks. It examines the ethical, regulatory, and practical challenges of ensuring transparency, accountability, and fairness in AI-driven sustainability initiatives. This book covers topics such as cybersecurity, international relations, and global trade, and is a useful resource for business owners, government officials, policymakers, engineers, academicians, researchers, and scientists. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于绿色金融与ESG领域的AI治理、法律与伦理，场景属于金融监管与可持续投资，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’的限定场景。
Justification_EN: The study addresses AI governance, law, and ethics in green finance and ESG—contexts of financial regulation and sustainable investment—not academic writing, research conduct, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication.

Title: Why Users Reject AI Counselors? The Mediating Role of Trust and Perceived Self-Correction Ability in Imperfect Experiences
Abstract: AI technology holds considerable promise in psychological counseling, but practical applications often encounter the challenge of algorithm aversion, particularly when users experience shortcomings with AI-driven counseling. This study conducted three experiments to investigate how such imperfect experiences might exacerbate algorithm aversion. Findings revealed that both subjective negative confirmation and objective imperfect counseling scenarios indirectly influenced user’s continued counseling intentions by moderating the relationship between the type of counselor (human vs. AI) and trust. The study also identified perceived differences in self-correction abilities between humans and AI as a potential factor contributing to algorithm aversion. Additionally, providing interpretive information about AI’s self-correction abilities was found to mitigate this aversion. The study not only advances our understanding of algorithm aversion mechanisms ‌but also carries significant ‌practical implications‌ for AI ethics training programs and digital mental health policy formulation. © 2025 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦AI在心理咨询服务中的用户接受度与算法厌恶问题，场景属于数字心理健康/临床应用，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’的限定场景，触犯排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: The study examines AI adoption and algorithm aversion in psychological counseling—a digital mental health application—falling outside the required academic publishing context (e.g., scholarly writing, peer review, journal publication), thus violating Exclusion Criterion 2.

Title: Mitigating Mental Health Disparities Through Predictive Analysis on Social Networks
Abstract: Mental health disparities in minority populations are not just a health issue but a complex interplay of cultural, economic, and systemic factors. These groups often encounter obstacles such as limited access to care, cultural stigma, and a lack of culturally competent resources, leading to underdiagnosed and undertreated conditions. Beyond traditional clinical settings, novel data analysis methods can be used to mitigate these challenges. Due to the continued growth of online social networks, there has been a plethora of information available, and this digital footprint is a significant data source to gain insights into solving the above challenge. Our research focuses on detection of mental health problems among underrepresented populations using predictive analytics on online social network data. By employing machine learning models and natural language processing, this research identifies behavioral markers and potential barriers to accessing mental health care. The findings emphasize the potential for AI-driven tools in reducing mental health disparities by facilitating targeted interventions in at-risk communities. This research further discusses ethical concerns related to AI-driven health assessments and highlights challenges for their responsible deployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽提及AI伦理问题，但其核心场景是AI在心理健康评估与公共卫生干预中的应用，属于医疗健康领域而非学术写作、期刊发表或学术出版场景，违反排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: Although the paper mentions ethical concerns of AI, its primary context is AI-driven mental health assessment and public health intervention—falling under clinical/healthcare ethics, not academic writing, journal publishing, or scholarly communication, thus violating Exclusion Criterion 2.

Title: Tech-Facilitated Disability Discrimination and Artificial Intelligence Tools at Work
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere and is particularly incorporated in every stage of employment, from hire to retire. This chapter emphasizes the ways in which the integration of these tools disproportionately impacts people with disabilities, focusing specifically on hiring tools, “bossware, " and wearable technologies in the workplace. It argues that digital accessibility ethics must be incorporated into corporate and HR ethics, particularly the principles of inclusion, privacy, transparency, and legal compliance. By incorporating this ethical framework into workplaces, employers can mitigate the potential harms of AI tools on disabled workers and create a more inclusive environment for all. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, Lainey Feingold, Reginé Gilbert, and Chancey Fleet; individual chapters, the contributors.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于职场中AI工具对残障人士的歧视性影响，属于劳动雇佣与数字可及性伦理范畴，不符合‘学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版’这一严格限定场景。
Justification_EN: The study addresses AI-facilitated disability discrimination in employment contexts (e.g., hiring tools and bossware), falling outside the required academic publishing domain—specifically excluding scholarly writing, research conduct, journal submission, peer review, or scholarly communication.

Title: Guided Safe Diffusion: Prohibiting Diffusion Models from Generating Inappropriate Content
Abstract: The increasing deployment of large generative models has heightened concerns over security and privacy, particularly regarding the generation of inappropriate content such as violent, explicit, or sensitive images, as well as the potential for creating fake images that spread misinformation and cause social problems. In this work, we propose Guided Safe Diffusion (GSD), an inference-time method specifically designed for diffusion models to prevent the generation of images with undesirable content as defined in a prohibited content list. Our method integrates safety guidance during the denoising steps of the model’s inference process, modifying the predicted noise to steer the generation process away from unwanted content. This approach allows the model to accept both an input image and a text description, facilitating controlled image generation. Unlike previous methods, our technique does not necessitate retraining or fine-tuning of the model. We conduct qualitative and quantitative experiments to assess the effectiveness of our method, demonstrating that GSD can remove the unwanted content while preserving unrelated content. The results validate our method’s ability to mitigate risks while maintaining the generative utility of diffusion models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于扩散模型在图像生成中的技术性安全控制（如禁止不当内容生成），未涉及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范中的AI伦理与披露问题，违反纳入标准第2、3条，且属于排除标准第1类（纯技术开发）。
Justification_EN: The paper addresses a technical safety mechanism for diffusion models in image generation without any engagement with AI ethics, disclosure requirements, academic writing, peer review, or scholarly publishing contexts, thus failing inclusion criteria 2 and 3 and falling under exclusion criterion 1.

Title: Guardrails, Not Guesswork: A Framework for Trustworthy AI Adoption
Abstract: Despite proliferating AI ethics frameworks and regulatory guidance, translating Responsible AI into organizational practice remains inconsistent, particularly among resource-constrained small- and mid-sized enterprises (SMEs) and public institutions. Existing models are either overly abstract or prohibitively resource-intensive. This paper advances a Lightweight Ethics-by-Design Playbook that operationalizes Responsible AI principles—fairness, accountability, transparency, and human oversight—into practical governance triggers, decision templates, and stage-specific checklists aligned with common organizational workflows. Unlike prevailing frameworks, this approach emphasizes scalability, accessibility, and sectoral adaptability without requiring technical infrastructure, empirical validation, or costly certification. By situating the playbook within regulatory debates and illustrating applications in healthcare, financial services, and government AI, the paper contributes a replicable, adoption-ready model bridging aspirational principles and actionable practice. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽涉及AI伦理与负责任AI实践，但其核心场景明确限定在医疗、金融和政府等非学术出版领域，且未提及学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或AI使用披露（AI Disclosure）等关键出版语境，违反排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: The paper focuses on AI adoption in healthcare, financial services, and government—non-academic publishing contexts—and makes no reference to scholarly writing, journal publication, peer review, or AI disclosure requirements, thus violating Exclusion Criterion 2.

Title: The Societal Implementation of Cybernetic Avatars and Regulatory Challenges in Society 5.0
Abstract: The societal integration of Cybernetic Avatars (CAs) presents a range of legal, ethical, and regulatory challenges. While CAs have the potential to enhance human capabilities and promote social inclusion, their implementation remains largely unregulated, particularly in Japan. This paper examines the legal complexities associated with CAs, focusing on the ambiguity of their legal status and the uncertainty surrounding liability attribution. It underscores the necessity of establishing a fundamental legal framework to address these issues. This study advocates for the creation of a dedicated legal structure modeled after Japan’s Barrier-Free Act, emphasizing the importance of ensuring equitable access and responsible governance. Additionally, it explores the potential enactment of a Cybernetic Avatar Social Inclusion Promotion Act, proposing policies aimed at fostering inclusive participation and mitigating associated risks. Furthermore, the ethical dimensions of CA-mediated interactions, including identity authentication, algorithmic bias, and personal data protection, are analyzed. Establishing a foundational legal framework to address these regulatory gaps is essential for facilitating the ethical integration of CAs while balancing technological innovation with legal and societal safeguards. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献聚焦于赛博格化身（Cybernetic Avatars）在社会5.0背景下的法律地位、责任归属、数据保护与社会包容等广义社会监管议题，未涉及人工智能在学术写作、期刊发表、同行评议或出版规范中的伦理问题或AI使用披露（AI Disclosure）。
Justification_EN: The paper addresses regulatory and ethical challenges of Cybernetic Avatars in societal governance, legal personhood, and data protection—outside the scope of AI use in academic writing, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication ethics and disclosure requirements.

Title: Deepfake Manipulation and Ethical Dilemmas: A Comprehensive Risk Assessment
Abstract: Deepfake technology, based on artificial intelligence (AI), enables the creation of realistic images, videos, and text, bringing new possibilities and posing serious ethical, social, and legal threats. The article examines key areas in which deepfakes affect contemporary society. This technology can be used to create false materials aimed at social destabilisation and propaganda, including disinformation. In the area of cyberbullying, deepfakes contribute to privacy violations such as pornography and blackmail. Additionally, generating false evidence can affect court decisions and facilitate financial fraud. This problem also affects the crisis of public trust, undermining the media’s credibility. The authors emphasise the need to introduce safeguards such as watermarking, public education and identification of AI-generated content. The need for international legal regulations and the development of technologies to detect deepfakes is indicated. The article considers ethical issues associated with this technology, minimising the risk of abuse and supporting innovation sustainably. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
Justification_ZH: 该文献虽涉及AI伦理问题，但其场景聚焦于社会安全、网络欺凌、司法证据和媒体信任等非学术出版领域，不符合‘场景明确限定在学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表、同行评议或学术出版领域’的纳入标准。
Justification_EN: Although the article addresses AI-related ethical issues, its context centers on societal security, cyberbullying, judicial evidence, and media credibility—outside the academic writing, research, journal publishing, peer review, or scholarly communication domain required by the inclusion criteria.

Title: AI Ethics in People Analytics: Balancing Automation, Privacy, and Fairness
Abstract: This chapter examines the synergistic relationship between cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI) as the core driver of modern digital transformation. It argues that while cloud computing provides the foundational infrastructure for organizational agility—enabling scalability, speed, and DevOps practices—it is the strategic application of AI that acts as the essential catalyst. AI transforms cloud capabilities into intelligent operations through predictive analytics, automation, and generative capabilities. The analysis moves from theoretical foundations to practical use cases across business functions, outlining the necessary human and organizational shifts. Crucially, the chapter concludes with a comprehensive discussion of the multi- faceted implications, addressing the managerial, practical, ethical, and social considerations leaders must navigate to harness this transformative potential responsibly and effectively. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.
Justification_ZH: 该文献主题为“人力分析（People Analytics）中的AI伦理”，聚焦组织管理场景下的自动化、隐私与公平问题，不属于学术写作、科学研究、期刊发表或同行评议等学术出版领域，违反纳入标准第3条且符合排除标准第2条。
Justification_EN: The study addresses AI ethics in people analytics—a business/HR management context focused on automation, privacy, and fairness—not in academic writing, research conduct, journal publishing, or peer review, thus failing inclusion criterion #3 and satisfying exclusion criterion #2.

Title: Optimizing Pedagogical Integrity Through AI Governance in Educational Ecosystems
Abstract: This chapter explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within education and its implications for pedagogical integrity, ethics, and governance. It examines how algorithmic systems influence learning processes, teacher agency, and educational equity. Drawing on theoretical traditions such as humanism, constructivism, and critical pedagogy, the study proposes the Ethical-AI Pedagogy Nexus (EAPN) framework to balance innovation with moral accountability. Through comparative policy analysis and globalcase studies, ithighlights best practices and failures across diverse educational systems. The chapter concludes that sustainable AI adoption requires participatory governance, ethical literacy, and continuous reflexivity to preserve autonomy, authenticity, and accountability in teaching and learning. Title: A New Era of Machine Intelligence in Education Industry: Towards a Sustainable Multifaceted Revolution
Abstract: The integration of Machine Intelligence into education systems represents a pivotal transformation in how knowledge is created, disseminated, and personalized. Going beyond the traditional bounds of Artificial Intelligence, MI integrates adaptive learning, cognitive computing, natural language processing, and emotional intelligence to build dynamic, learner-centred ecosystems. The chapter discusses the historical overview of educational paradigms, theoretical frameworks for understanding MI in the educational context, and highlighting its distinction from conventional AI and ML paradigms. MI enhances curriculum development, enables intelligent content delivery, supports learner modeling at scale, and revolutionizes assessment and feedback mechanisms through automation and predictive analytics. Thus, the chapter also delves into the augmentation of teaching roles via AI-based assistants and institutional decision-making through intelligent administration. It further discusses how generative AI is reshaping curriculum design and enabling adaptive learning platforms. Key challenges around policy, governance, ethics, and standardization are critically assessed, with special focus on the role of government bodies and international organizations. Finally, the chapter discusses a new perspective on different ways MI can contribute to equitable, sustainable, and future-ready education systems. © 2026 Amit Kumar Tyagi.
